acts.desc: Former Bush Administration official David Frum explains a very surprising fact about Bush's economic failure, as it relates to health care. Frum is a regular contributor to the radio show Marketplace.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: Are doctors to blame for the rising costs? NPR Science Correspondent Alix Spiegel reports on the shocking results of studies about varied health care spending. Hear more health care stories this week from Alix at npr.org.
acts.title: Dartmouth Atlas Shrugged

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: Or is the problem the patients? Producer Lisa Pollak reports.
acts.title: Every Cat Scan Has Nine Lives

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Or maybe the insurance companies are to blame? Producer Sarah Koenig reports.
acts.title: Who Would Win In A Fight Between A Polar Bear And An Insurance Company?

acts.label: Act Four
acts.desc: Host Ira Glass talks with Susan Dentzer, editor of the journal Health Affairs, about what current health reform proposals do to fix the rising costs of healthcare...And points at a surprising, kind of heartening phenomenon happening within the current debate.
acts.title: Now What?
